independent_prior_note: ρ_T = 20.0 g/cm³ from GNSS atomic clock correlations (Paper 6, UCD) (independent prior from terrestrial geodesy)

volumetric_prediction.caveat: Effective observable-response band only: the mediated-force decomposition is product-limited by the screened solar source charge and returns ≲10⁻⁹–10⁻⁸, so the quoted band cannot be a charge×charge differential-fall estimate. It is additionally superseded by the canonical pairwise operator (Paper 0 v0.15, Appendix E R11), which suppresses the Earth-Moon force channel to ~10⁻¹⁴.

source_charge_product_limit.verdict: Under any mediated-force reading the differential-fall observable is bounded by ≲10⁻⁹–10⁻⁸ — five orders below the measured 10⁻⁴ band. The volumetric α_eff can be read only as an effective response coefficient (all factors folded in), not as a body coupling; the 'distinct projection' exemption from the source-charge bound is not available to a force channel.

conclusions.explanation: The simulation calculates Earth and Moon shielding factors from density profiles using ρ_T. The shielding differential quantifies the differential degree of Temporal Topology flattening between the two interiors. The volumetric suppression model yields an effective η band ≈ α_eff^(Earth-Moon) Δ⟨(ρ/ρ_T)^3⟩ ≈ -10⁻⁴ in the observed decade, but as a mediated-force estimate it is internally inconsistent: folding in the Cassini-bounded solar source charge gives ≲10⁻⁹–10⁻⁸, and the canonical pairwise operator independently suppresses the force channel to ~10⁻¹⁴. The surviving admissible channel for the measured residual is the clock-sector/ephemeris-reduction projection (Section 2.1), whose amplitude map is the open estimand question of the source-level integrator refit. η itself is the observable response coefficient for LLR, not derived from κ_LL.
